This is a **finding** in the frozen reference driver (no files modified).

### Cause
- When a patient with `verbosity == "rambling"` confirms a read-back, [Voice._clear_yes](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L91-L99) returns `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` (7 word tokens).
- In [DcitlF](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L34) (`CONSENT_IN_CODE = True`), [Driver.book](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L490) first checks [explicit_confirm](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), which requires `len(re.findall(r"\w+", t)) <= 4` for `yes`/`yep`/`yeah`/`confirmed` phrases (unless `"i confirm"` appears), so it returns `None` for the 7-word reply.
- [Driver.consent](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271) then discards any model `"yes"` because `self.consent_in_code` is `True`, returning `None`; [Driver.unclear](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306) re-asks once (`"Please reply yes or no: book ..."`), and on the patient's second identical reply (`n >= 2`) queues a staff hand-off without booking.

This is a **finding** in the frozen reference driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py) and [dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py)):

1. In [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L91-L99), `Voice._clear_yes` produces `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` when `verbosity == "rambling"`.
2. In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), `explicit_confirm` only returns `True` for `^(yes|yep|yeah|confirmed)\b` when `len(re.findall(r"\w+", t)) <= 4`. Because `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` has 7 `\w+` tokens, `explicit_confirm` returns `None`.
3. In `Driver.book` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L493)), `c is None` falls through to `Driver.consent` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271)). Under Arm F (`CONSENT_IN_CODE = True` in [dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L33)), `Driver.consent` ignores a model `"yes"` and returns `None`, so `Driver.unclear` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306)) re-asks `"Please reply yes or no: book ...?"`.
4. When the patient repeats `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."`, `explicit_confirm` and `Driver.consent` return `None` again, `Driver.unclear` hits `n >= 2` and queues a hand-off, and `DcitlF.turn` calls `self.api.hand_off("confirm")` with nothing booked.

The failure occurs because both the driver and the instrument behave as designed, and Arm F's consent-in-code design rejects a valid multi-word confirmation:

1. In [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L91-L99), `Voice._clear_yes` returns `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` for a clear `accept` when `verbosity == "rambling"`.
2. In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), `explicit_confirm` only accepts `yes`/`yep`/`yeah`/`confirmed` when `len(re.findall(r"\w+", t)) <= 4`. `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` has 7 `\w+` tokens (`yes`, `that`, `s`, `right`, `please`, `go`, `ahead`), so `explicit_confirm` returns `None`.
3. Under Arm F ([dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L24), `CONSENT_IN_CODE = True`), `Driver.consent` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271)) treats any model `"yes"` as `None`, so `Driver.book` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L490)) calls `Driver.unclear("confirm", ...)` to re-ask `"Please reply yes or no: ..."`. When the patient repeats `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."`, `Driver.unclear` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306)) reaches `n >= 2` and hands off to staff with nothing booked. (Arm F2 in [dcitl_f2.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f2.py#L16-L27) avoids this by replacing `explicit_confirm` with `clear_confirm`, which has no 4-word cap.)

hypotheses.cause: In Arm F (consent_in_code=True), Driver.consent ignores model 'yes' answers, so confirmation relies solely on explicit_confirm, which rejects 'Yes, that's right, please go ahead.' because it exceeds the 4-word limit. After re-asking once and getting the same reply, Driver.unclear hits n >= 2 and hands off to staff with nothing booked.

In clinicbench.adapters.dcitl_port.explicit_confirm, the 4-word token limit (len(re.findall(r"\w+", t)) <= 4) causes "Yes, that's right, please go ahead." (7 tokens) to return None. Under Arm F (consent_in_code=True), Driver.consent also returns None for a model "yes", so two consecutive replies trigger Driver.unclear's hand-off with nothing booked.

For rambling patients, Voice._clear_yes emits the 7-token confirmation "Yes, that's right, please go ahead.", which exceeds explicit_confirm's 4-word limit and returns None. Because Arm F's consent-in-code design discards a model "yes" in Driver.consent, Driver.book re-asks once via Driver.unclear and then hands off to staff on the second identical reply.
